title: Third-order nonlinear transport in a percolative two-dimensional superconductor
authors: Wenjun Liu, Chenghe Wang, Xiubin Li, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Tao Zhang, Xiao-Xiao Zhang, Jing Li
abstract: Percolative superconductivity frequently arises in two-dimensional van der Waals materials due to reduced dimensionality, enhanced quantum fluctuations, and complex electron-phonon interactions, providing a unique platform where normal electrons coexist with Cooper pairs. We report the observation of substantial third-order nonlinear transport in a trilayer $1T^\prime$-MoTe$_2$ superconductor within its percolative transition regime. The third-harmonic longitudinal voltage ($V_{\|}^{3ω}$) exhibits a clear cubic dependence on excitation current below a threshold, with both its magnitude and nonlinear coefficient strongly correlated with the superconducting state. This nonlinear response is semiquantitatively captured by the superconducting fluctuation within the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory, where nonlinear transport arises due to fluctuating Cooper pairs. Our results demonstrate that third-order nonlinear transport serves as a sensitive probe of superconducting transitions in percolative systems and establish a foundation for exploring higher-order transport phenomena in strongly correlated systems.
summary: This work reports observing third-order nonlinear electrical transport in a percolative superconductor ($	ext{MoTe}_2$), demonstrating that this nonlinearity is highly sensitive to the superconducting state. By correlating the measured cubic voltage response with theoretical predictions from Ginzburg-Landau theory, the authors establish higher-order transport as a powerful diagnostic tool for studying superconducting fluctuations in low-dimensional materials.
main_problem: The study investigates third-order nonlinear transport as a sensitive probe for superconducting transitions occurring in percolative two-dimensional superconductors.
main_result: A clear cubic dependence of the third-harmonic voltage on current was observed, and this nonlinearity was found to be strongly correlated with the superconducting state, vanishing near the transition temperature.
method: The research combines low-frequency lock-in measurements of nonlinear voltages ($V_{3\omega}$) with theoretical modeling based on time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory.
model_or_system: The physical system is a trilayer $1T'$-MoTe$_2$ superconductor operating in its percolative transition regime. The analysis utilizes superconducting fluctuation models derived from the Ginzburg-Landau framework to explain the observed nonlinear response.
key_observables: Third-harmonic longitudinal voltage ($V_{3\omega\parallel}$), third-order transport coefficient ($\alpha^*$), and subcritical current scale ($I^*$).
important_parameters: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c \approx 1.4$ K), excitation current ($I$), perpendicular magnetic field ($B_{\perp}$), and back gate voltage ($V_{BG}$).
main_assumptions: The nonlinear response is assumed to originate from fluctuating Cooper pairs, which is semi-quantitatively captured by the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory.
figures_summary: Figures demonstrate the cubic dependence of $V_{3\omega\parallel}$ on current at various temperatures and gate voltages. They also map out how $\alpha^*$ and $I^*$ change systematically with temperature, magnetic field, and doping (gate voltage).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the experimental setup and measures nonlinear transport across different regimes (T, B, V_BG). It then correlates the measured third-order coefficients ($\alpha^*$) with superconducting fluctuations predicted by GL theory, confirming its utility as a sensitive probe.
why_interesting: The strong correlation between higher-order non-linear response and superconducting fluctuations provides an experimental handle to study pairing mechanisms and coherence in strongly correlated 2D materials without relying solely on transport measurements near zero resistance.
